why: The matrix the statement fixes, unchanged.
Addition of matrices, on both sides.
The scalar $\tau$ times the matrix. `•` is `SMul`, which for `Matrix I J ℝ` is the entrywise scalar multiple the paper means.

$e_s e_j^{\mathsf T}$ is the outer product of two standard basis vectors: the matrix with a single 1 in position $(s,j)$ and zeros elsewhere. That matrix is `Matrix.single s j 1`. The paper names it by a construction and Mathlib by what it is, so this edge is the one place in the step where the two notations genuinely differ — which is why it is worth its own level.
The closing `$` of the inline formula.
